claims.text: Sequence-level probability estimates given by LLMs have limitations as reliable indicators of generation quality.
LLMs demonstrate strong calibration at the token level when choosing correct answers in multiple-choice questions or evaluating true/false statements.
Self-evaluation based scoring methods improve selective generation accuracy in LLMs.
Self-evaluation based scores correlate better with the overall quality of generated content than probability-based metrics.

evidence.description: Experiments using PaLM-2 and GPT-3 on TruthfulQA and TL;DR benchmarks show accuracy improvements in selective generation when using self-evaluation.
Empirical evaluation on TruthfulQA and TL;DR using PaLM-2 and GPT-3 demonstrated higher correlation between self-evaluation scores and overall quality.

methodologies.name: Token-level Self-Evaluation for Selective Generation
methodologies.description: Open-ended generation tasks are reformulated into token-level prediction tasks where an LLM self-evaluates its answers using multi-way comparison or point-wise evaluation.

limitations.text: Sequence-level probability estimates (such as perplexity) are limited as reliable indicators of generation quality.
